output.brief: The jump in write-offs is mostly self-inflicted. Since the night receiving team was cut from six to four (week 31), night chilled pallets take about 3h50 to reach the chambers, up from 44 minutes. Dock lanes are unrefrigerated at 15–17°C. Night write-offs rose from 0.6% to 2.9%, while day write-offs stayed flat. The rise is the same for Haverlow, Pellridge and own-label, so it is not a Haverlow problem. Haverlow's trailer data, which can't be edited, shows loads arriving at 2.4–3.5°C and unloaded by about 23:30. The warm receipt readings were taken around 03:00, after the pallets had sat on the dock. Chambers held temperature. Don't raise the chargeback or shift volume: the evidence contradicts it. Dropping the night probe would hide the problem. Lead with restoring night receiving to six and setting a maximum dock-to-chamber time, tracked weekly from scan data. Separately, pull Corriebank's claim-level data to test over-claiming. That is plausible, since credits rose after self-certification began, but it is unproven. Confidence is high on the main cause and moderate on the credits.
